libraryDocuments.title: Direct student task evidence
libraryDocuments.content: SYNTHETIC FIXTURE, NOT A REAL PAPER. An experiment compared university students after acute total sleep deprivation and a normal-sleep condition. Spatial-span task performance was lower in the deprivation condition. No phonological-loop component, grades or downstream academic outcomes were measured. Sample size, effect size and statistical details are unknown in this excerpt.

libraryDocuments.title: Soldiers and N-back
libraryDocuments.content: SYNTHETIC FIXTURE, NOT A REAL PAPER. Soldiers completed an N-back task after acute total sleep deprivation. Task responses were slower. The excerpt does not establish a phonological-loop mechanism or university-student effects.

libraryDocuments.title: Animal reversal learning
libraryDocuments.content: SYNTHETIC FIXTURE, NOT A REAL PAPER. Rats completed reversal-learning tasks after disrupted sleep. Reversal-learning performance was worse. Human visuospatial working memory was not measured.

libraryDocuments.title: Conflicting student task finding
libraryDocuments.content: SYNTHETIC FIXTURE, NOT A REAL PAPER. A university-student study under repeated partial sleep restriction reported no detectable change on its N-back outcome. This null task result is relevant to the argument, but it does not prove absence of every possible effect. The excerpt supplies no power calculation or effect size.

libraryDocuments.title: Vigilance proxy
libraryDocuments.content: SYNTHETIC FIXTURE, NOT A REAL PAPER. Esports players reporting poor sleep quality had lower vigilance-task performance in an observational comparison. Working memory and grades were not measured. The exposure differs from acute total deprivation and repeated partial restriction.
